symbols.name: V
symbols.def: The finite substantive-variable set of the labeled-missingness system.

symbols.name: R
symbols.type: finite set of binary missingness indicators
symbols.def: The indicators whose value zero denotes that the corresponding partially observed substantive variable is missing.

symbols.name: Vdag
symbols.type: finite set of observed proxy variables
symbols.def: The proxy copy of each partially observed variable, equal to its substantive value when observed and to the missing symbol otherwise.

symbols.name: O
symbols.def: The complete observed record consisting of always-observed substantive variables, proxies, and missingness indicators.

symbols.name: Xspace
symbols.def: The finite alphabet assigned to each substantive, indicator, and proxy variable.

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: The treatment whose natural causal effect is queried.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: The outcome of the intervention on \(A\).

symbols.name: sY
symbols.def: A supplied real-valued coding of the finite outcome alphabet used to form the natural average treatment contrast.

symbols.name: a0
symbols.def: The reference treatment value \(a_0\).

symbols.name: a1
symbols.def: The active treatment value \(a_1\), distinct from \(a_0\).

symbols.name: G
symbols.def: A known finite labeled-missingness graph whose directed part is acyclic, whose bidirected edges encode latent districts, and whose label set records the missingness contexts in which directed edges are absent.

symbols.name: Hlog
symbols.type: finite set of always-observed pre-treatment logistics variables
symbols.def: A nonempty always-observed DAG block whose only arrows to vertices outside the block enter the missingness indicator \(R_W\).

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: A member of \(H\) with the arrow \(C\to R_W\).

symbols.name: Bchain
symbols.type: finite chain of always-observed mediator variables
symbols.def: The mediator chain \(A\to B_1\to\cdots\to B_m\to Y\) used by the endogenous-indicator proxy front-door family.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: A semi-Markovian finite-state structural model compatible with \(\mathcal G\), with one mutually independent latent factor for each individual bidirected edge and one private factor for each vertex, including its proxy equations and label-specific mechanism deletions.

symbols.name: Mlm
symbols.def: The de Aguas--Henckel--Pensar--Biele class of finite semi-Markovian labeled-missingness SCMs inducing \(\mathcal G\).

symbols.name: Mplus
symbols.def: The finite strictly positive regular-maximal subclass of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G)\) used by the recovery problem.

symbols.name: Pobs
symbols.def: A population law of the observed record \(\mathcal O\).

symbols.name: pCell
symbols.def: Algebraically independent real variables subject to the observed-simplex and compatibility formulas; specialization sets \(p_o=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o)\).

symbols.name: ExactObs
symbols.def: Either rational observed cells, real-algebraic observed cells given by square-free integer polynomials and rational isolating intervals, or an exact-real oracle that decides the sign of every integer polynomial at the observed-cell vector.

symbols.name: Fiber
symbols.def: The models in \(\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\) that induce the same observed proxy law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

symbols.name: Qa
symbols.def: The natural interventional distribution of \(Y\) under treatment value \(a\), retaining the endogenous missingness mechanism shifts.

symbols.name: tau
symbols.def: The score-coded natural average treatment effect obtained from the two interventional outcome laws.

symbols.name: kappa
symbols.def: A current CADMG \(\mathcal H\), fixed set \(F\), context assignment \(c\), kernel \(q\), observed-law provenance expression \(\pi\), and ordered label-license trace \(\Lambda\).

symbols.name: Fix
symbols.def: The nested fixing update for a vertex \(v\), tagged by the label license \(\lambda\) and retaining its pre-restriction observed-law trace.

symbols.name: Select
symbols.def: The update that restricts a trace-aware state to missingness context \(c\) only after recording every kernel factor derived before restriction.

symbols.name: Swap
symbols.def: The primitive adjacent-swap condition that \(u\) and \(v\) are both fixable in \(\mathcal H\), neither is an ancestor of a missingness variable appearing in the other's license, and both denominator traces are supported before the same context restriction.

symbols.name: LatentIndex
symbols.def: One factor index for each individual bidirected edge of \(\mathcal G\), plus one private factor for each substantive or missingness vertex; all indexed factors are mutually independent.

symbols.name: Krf
symbols.def: Here \(N_{\mathcal G}=\sum_{Z\in\mathcal V\cup\mathcal R}|\mathcal X_Z|\prod_{X\in\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G}(Z)}|\mathcal X_X|\prod_{R_X\in\mathcal R}(|\mathcal X_{R_X}|+1)\); every edge and private latent factor is assigned the alphabet \(\{1,\ldots,K_{\mathcal G}\}\).

symbols.name: Resp
symbols.type: finite set of label-compatible vertex response-table tuples
symbols.def: Each \(g=(g_Z)_Z\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}\) is a tuple of deterministic maps from the observed-parent values, the private latent state, and the states of the individual bidirected-edge factors incident to \(Z\) into \(\mathcal X_Z\), with table entries identified exactly when a graph label requires an observed parent to be omitted in that context.

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: Real variables constrained by \(\gamma_g^2-\gamma_g=0\) and \(\sum_g\gamma_g=1\), so exactly one label-compatible structural-table tuple is selected and no mixture across graph-wide tables is introduced.

symbols.name: rho
symbols.sig: \(\rho=(\rho_{h,k}:h\in\mathcal E^{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal G)\sqcup\mathcal V\sqcup\mathcal R,\ 1\leq k\leq K_{\mathcal G})\)
symbols.def: For every individual bidirected-edge or private factor \(h\), the coordinates satisfy \(\rho_{h,k}\geq0\) and \(\sum_k\rho_{h,k}=1\); the probability of a joint latent state is the product over \(h\).

symbols.name: theta
symbols.def: The one-hot table selectors together with the mutually independent individual-edge and private-factor weights.

symbols.name: pRF
symbols.def: The sum over the finite latent-factor states and selected structural table of the product \(\gamma_g\prod_h\rho_{h,u_h}\) when deterministic evaluation gives full-data cell \((v,r)\), and its proxy-consistent sum over cells mapping to observed cell \(o\).

symbols.name: qRF
symbols.def: The same independent-factor polynomial sum after replacing the selected response equation for \(A\) by the constant \(a\) and summing all remaining finite cells with \(Y=y\).

symbols.name: Compat
symbols.def: The conjunction of one-hot table equations, one simplex for every individual latent factor, strict positivity of every full-data cell polynomial, and the equalities \(p_o(\theta)=p_o\) for all observed cells.

symbols.name: ConstTest
symbols.type: first-order real-closed-field formula with observed-law parameters
symbols.def: The first-order real-closed-field formula denying two \(\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\cdot;\mathbf p)\)-compatible response vectors with unequal \(q_{a,y}\) values, leaving only \(\mathbf p\) free.

symbols.name: SemiPart
symbols.def: A finite family of pairwise-disjoint quantifier-free sign formulas whose union is the compatible observed-law projection and whose cells carry, for every \(a,y\), either a unique-value graph formula or a non-singleton-fiber witness formula.

symbols.name: AlgPair
symbols.def: On a negative partition cell, the compatibility conjunction for two response vectors together with \(q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1)\); exact specialization yields a sample \(\omega=(a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\) represented by Thom encodings over the ordered field generated by \(\mathbf p\), and the coordinates are real algebraic when the observed cells are rational or real algebraic.

symbols.name: TCF
symbols.def: The observed-law-indexed trace-aware colored fixing compiler that treats the cells of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) as formal coordinates \(\mathbf p\) and returns the finite semialgebraic decision object \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\); an exact-law specialization selects a unique cell and yields its functional or algebraic witness formula. Colored hedges are not part of this output contract.

symbols.name: Fobs
symbols.def: On an identifying cell of \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\), either a rational trace expression or the unique real-algebraic value whose graph is specified by a quantifier-free polynomial formula; exact specialization uses isolating data only when needed.

symbols.name: DA4
symbols.type: set of de Aguas Proposition 4 certificates
symbols.def: The triples \(\xi=(K,H,\{L_r:r\in\operatorname{supp}(R_K)\})\) satisfying Proposition 4 conditions \(\mathrm{(i)}\)--\(\mathrm{(v)}\) in the labeled graphs \(\mathcal G_r\) and \(\mathcal H_r\).

symbols.name: FDA4
symbols.def: The published weighted context formula \(\sum_r P_{\mathrm{obs}}(R_K=r)\sum_{\ell}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(L_r^{\dagger}=\ell\mid R_K=r,R_{M_r}=1)P_{\mathrm{obs}}(Y=y\mid A=a,L_r^{\dagger}=\ell,R_K=r,R_{M_r}=1,R_H=0)\).

symbols.name: RootCtx
symbols.def: A certificate that every label context variable is an observed causal root and that the Mokhtarian--Jamshidi--Etesami--Kiyavash context-by-context algorithm identifies the interventional law in every context DAG.

symbols.name: FRoot
symbols.def: The sum over root-control contexts of the published context-specific ID functional multiplied by the observed probability of that context.

symbols.name: CH
symbols.def: The nested rooted-forest obstructions equipped with compatible missingness colors and complete observed-trace provenance.

symbols.name: Divergence
symbols.def: A testable predicate requiring agreement of all proper-predecessor trace polynomials, \(D\subsetneq D'\), equal roots ancestral to \(Y\) after intervention, \(D\cap A=\varnothing\), \(D'\cap A\neq\varnothing\), and persistence of the query-polynomial difference after marginalizing outside \(D'\). It does not assert that a qualifying record exists or implies a colored hedge.

symbols.name: Compiler
symbols.def: A finite syntax-directed procedure that decodes the two edge-factorized response models and returns either the first retained-history record passing the candidate divergence tests or an exhaustion tag. It does not return or certify a colored hedge.

symbols.name: M0
symbols.def: The first edge-factorized response model decoded from an exact negative-cell sample.

symbols.name: M1
symbols.def: The second edge-factorized response model decoded from an exact negative-cell sample.

symbols.name: GFig
symbols.def: The de Aguas et al. Figure 3(b) graph with \(R_W\to A\), \(Z\to A\), \(Z\to W\), \(W\to A\) labeled by \(R_W=0\), \(W\leftrightarrow Y\), \(R_Z\leftrightarrow Y\), and \(A\to Y\).

symbols.name: PFig
symbols.type: observed proxy law on the Figure 3(b) graph
symbols.def: A strictly positive observed law compatible with \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{3b}}\).

symbols.name: GEIP
symbols.def: The parameterized family obtained from the Figure 3(b) fix-before-select module by adding a nonempty always-observed logistics DAG \(H\) with an arrow \(C\to R_W\), replacing \(A\to Y\) by the mediator chain \(A\to B_1\to\cdots\to B_m\to Y\), and adding \(A\leftrightarrow Y\).

symbols.name: GStar
symbols.def: The member with one logistics parent \(C\to R_W\), one mediator \(A\to B_1\to Y\), the Figure 3(b) edges and proxy mechanism, and the added edge \(A\leftrightarrow Y\).

symbols.name: FStar
symbols.def: The observed-law functional obtained by averaging the conditional front-door formula in context \(R_W=0\) over the marginal law of \(C\).

symbols.name: Size
symbols.def: Here \(n=|\mathcal V\cup\mathcal R\cup\mathcal V^{\dagger}|\), \(\ell=|\mathcal L|\), \(c=\prod_{R_Z\in\mathcal R}(|\mathcal X_{R_Z}|+1)\), \(h=|\mathcal E^{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal G)|+|\mathcal V|+|\mathcal R|\), \(g=|\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}|\), \(K_{\mathcal G}\) is the latent support bound, \(p=2\{g+hK_{\mathcal G}\}+|\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}|\), and \(s\) is the complete binary encoding length of the partition-generating part of one terminal \((a,y)\)-package, including polynomial counts, degrees, integer coefficients, variable indices, Boolean connectives, and the names of all free observed cells.

symbols.name: CADsteps
symbols.def: For a fixed signed-subresultant cylindrical-algebraic-decomposition implementation, the maximum of its number of projection, real-root-isolation, sign-evaluation steps and output cells over real-closed-field formulas with at most \(m\) total quantified-plus-free variables and binary encoding length at most \(b\).

symbols.name: eps
symbols.def: The probability used by a label-preserving response randomization when strict positivity is imposed on a finite witness.

symbols.name: RFHandle
symbols.def: The label-respecting response-function encoding attached to a colored hedge and a positivity parameter.

assumptions.condition: \(|\mathcal X_Z|<\infty\) for every \(Z\in\mathcal V\cup\mathcal R\cup\mathcal V^{\dagger}\).
The directed part of \(\mathcal G\) is acyclic.

\(\mathcal M\) has one exogenous factor shared by the two endpoints of each bidirected edge of \(\mathcal G\), one private exogenous factor for each substantive or missingness vertex, and all these factors are mutually independent.
For every partially observed \(Z\in\mathcal V\), \(Z^{\dagger}=Z\) when \(R_Z=1\) and \(Z^{\dagger}=\star\) when \(R_Z=0\).
Every label \((X,Z,R_X=0)\) in \(\mathcal G\) encodes that the structural mechanism for \(Z\) omits \(X\) in context \(R_X=0\).
The label set of \(\mathcal G\) is regular.
The label set of \(\mathcal G\) is maximal.
\(P_{\mathcal M}(v,r)>0\) for every \((v,r)\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\).

standard.name: strict positivity for finite causal laws

definitions.name: Published labeled-missingness SCM class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G)=\{\mathcal M:\mathcal M\text{ is a finite-state semi-Markovian lm-SCM inducing }\mathcal G\text{ and satisfying the proxy and label semantics}\}\).

definitions.name: Positive regular-maximal labeled-missingness class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G):|\mathcal X_Z|<\infty\text{ for every }Z\in\mathcal V\cup\mathcal R\cup\mathcal V^{\dagger},\ \mathcal G\text{ is regular and maximal},\ P_{\mathcal M}(v,r)>0\text{ for every }(v,r)\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\}\).

definitions.name: Observed-proxy-law fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G):P_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}\}\).

definitions.name: Natural interventional law and contrast
definitions.construction: For \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), set \(Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)=P_{\mathcal M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))\), and set \(\tau_{s_Y}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)\{Q_{a_1}^{\mathcal M}(y)-Q_{a_0}^{\mathcal M}(y)\}\).

definitions.name: Edge-factorized finite response-function polynomial fiber
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathcal J=\mathcal E^{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal G)\sqcup\mathcal V\sqcup\mathcal R\). For \(g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}\) introduce \(\gamma_g\), and for \(h\in\mathcal J\) and \(1\leq k\leq K_{\mathcal G}\) introduce \(\rho_{h,k}\). For a full cell \((v,r)\), define \[p_{v,r}(\theta)=\sum_{g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}}\sum_{u\in\{1,\ldots,K_{\mathcal G}\}^{\mathcal J}}\mathbf 1\{g(u)=(v,r)\}\gamma_g\prod_{h\in\mathcal J}\rho_{h,u_h},\qquad p_o(\theta)=\sum_{(v,r):\operatorname{proxy}(v,r)=o}p_{v,r}(\theta).\] Define \(q_{a,y}(\theta)\) by the same sum with the equation for \(A\) replaced by \(a\). With formal coordinates \(\mathbf p=(p_o)_o\), define \[\begin{aligned}\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p):={}&\bigwedge_{g\in\mathcal T_{\mathcal G}}(\gamma_g^2-\gamma_g=0)\ \wedge\ \sum_g\gamma_g=1\ \wedge\ \bigwedge_{h\in\mathcal J}\left(\bigwedge_{k=1}^{K_{\mathcal G}}\rho_{h,k}\geq0\ \wedge\ \sum_{k=1}^{K_{\mathcal G}}\rho_{h,k}=1\right)\\&\wedge\bigwedge_{(v,r)}p_{v,r}(\theta)>0\ \wedge\ \bigwedge_{o\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}}p_o(\theta)=p_o.\end{aligned}\] The product over individual edge and private factors enforces the published semi-Markovian independence structure, while the one-hot equations encode a finite union over fixed structural tables rather than a graph-wide latent mixture.

definitions.name: Symbolic terminal real-closed-field constancy test
definitions.construction: For every \(a\in\mathcal X_A\) and \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), use disjoint copies \(\theta^0=(\gamma^0,\rho^0)\) and \(\theta^1=(\gamma^1,\rho^1)\) and eliminate precisely those response variables from \[\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p):=\neg\exists\theta^0\,\exists\theta^1\left[\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^0;\mathbf p)\wedge\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta^1;\mathbf p)\wedge q_{a,y}(\theta^0)\neq q_{a,y}(\theta^1)\right].\] The only free variables are the \(|\mathcal X_{\mathcal O}|\) coordinates \(\mathbf p\). Quantifier elimination returns a quantifier-free sign formula, not a numerical decision at an arbitrary population law. On its true region the value relation is \[\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z):=\exists\theta\left[\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\wedge z=q_{a,y}(\theta)\right],\] which has exactly one \(z\); on its false region the certificate formula is the unnegated doubled conjunction. A sample pair is extracted only after an exact specialization.

definitions.name: Symbolic observed-law decision partition
definitions.construction: Conjoin the simplex formula \(p_o\geq0\), \(\sum_op_o=1\), and the feasible-projection formula \(\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\) with every quantifier-free output of \(\mathsf I_{a,y}\), refine their common sign-invariant CAD, and discard infeasible cells. The remaining pairwise-disjoint formulas \(\psi_1(\mathbf p),\ldots,\psi_J(\mathbf p)\) form \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\). Each cell stores, for every \(a,y\), either the unique-value relation \(\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z)\) or the witness relation \(\mathsf W_j(\mathbf p,a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\).

definitions.name: Exact observed-law specialization
definitions.construction: Given \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), decide the finitely many integer-polynomial signs in \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\) using rational arithmetic, algebraic-number arithmetic with the supplied square-free polynomials and isolating intervals, or the supplied exact-real sign oracle. Choose the unique cell containing \(p_o=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o)\). On an identifying cell, represent its unique value \(z\), and on a negative cell choose \(\theta^0,\theta^1\) satisfying \(\mathsf W_j\), by Thom encodings over the real closure of the ordered field generated by the specialized coordinates \(\mathbf p\). These response coordinates are algebraic over that ordered input field; they are real algebraic over \(\mathbb Q\) when the observed cells are rational or real algebraic, but no such claim is made for transcendental exact-real cells. No operation on an arbitrary unencoded population real is defined.

definitions.name: Published Proposition 4 certificate and functional
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{DA4}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) consists of every \(\xi=(K,H,\{L_r\}_r)\) satisfying de Aguas et al. Proposition 4 conditions \(\mathrm{(i)}\)--\(\mathrm{(v)}\): the inclusion and exclusion rule for \(L_r\), the no-descendant condition in \(\mathcal G_r\), and the three stated d-separations in \(\mathcal G_r[\overline A]\) and \(\mathcal H_r[\underline A]\). For such \(\xi\), \[f^{\mathrm{DA4}}_{a,\xi}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=\sum_{r\in\operatorname{supp}(R_K)}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(R_K=r)\sum_{\ell}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(L_r^{\dagger}=\ell\mid R_K=r,R_{M_r}=1)P_{\mathrm{obs}}(Y=y\mid A=a,L_r^{\dagger}=\ell,R_K=r,R_{M_r}=1,R_H=0).\]

definitions.name: Published root-control certificate and functional
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) holds when every label context variable is observed and parentless and the published context-specific algorithm returns \(f_{a,c}^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\) in every context \(c\). Its published aggregate is \[f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=\sum_c P_{\mathrm{obs}}(C=c)f_{a,c}^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y).\]

definitions.name: Trace-aware colored reachable state
definitions.construction: \(\kappa=(\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda)\), where \(\mathcal H\) is the current CADMG, \(F\) is its fixed set, \(c\) is a partial assignment to missingness indicators, \(q\) is a normalized kernel on the random vertices of \(\mathcal H\), \(\pi\) is a finite expression in observed cells of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \(\Lambda\) is an ordered list of pairs consisting of a label license and the pre-restriction trace that licensed it.

definitions.name: Licensed colored fixing
definitions.construction: If \(v\) is fixable in \(\mathcal H\) and license \(\lambda\) is valid on the trace recorded by \(\kappa\), \(\Phi_v^{\lambda}\) moves \(v\) from the random to the fixed set, deletes arrowheads into \(v\), replaces \(q\) by \(q/q(v\mid\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal H}(v))\), applies the same division to \(\pi\), and appends \(\lambda\) and its current provenance to \(\Lambda\).

definitions.name: Delayed context restriction
definitions.construction: For a missingness assignment \(c'\) compatible with the current trace, \(\Sigma_{c'}(\kappa)\) restricts \(q\) and \(\pi\) to \(c'\), normalizes on the positive selected cell, deletes the edges carrying labels activated by \(c'\), and retains every earlier entry of \(\Lambda\).

definitions.name: Primitive colored adjacent-swap condition
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Swap}_{\kappa}(u,v)\) holds exactly when \(u\) and \(v\) are both fixable in the current \(\mathcal H\), \(u\notin\operatorname{an}_{\mathcal H}(C_v)\), \(v\notin\operatorname{an}_{\mathcal H}(C_u)\), the license contexts \(C_u\) and \(C_v\) agree on their common indicators, and both fixing denominators are supported in the same pre-restriction trace.

definitions.name: Trace-colored hedge
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) is the set of tuples \((\mathcal F,\mathcal F',\chi,T)\) such that \(\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F\) are equally rooted \(C\)-forests, \(\mathcal F\cap A\neq\varnothing\), \(\mathcal F'\cap A=\varnothing\), their roots are ancestors of \(Y\) after intervention on \(A\), \(\chi\) assigns every label-sensitive edge its missingness context, and \(T\) is a prefix-closed collection of observed traces on which every color used by the two forests is licensed.

definitions.name: Algebraic-witness diagnostic compiler
definitions.construction: Given an exact specialized negative-cell witness \(\omega=(a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\) and a finite retained operation history \(\mathcal T\), first decode \(\theta^0,\theta^1\) through their selected response tables and product laws over the individual edge and private factors, obtaining \(\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\). Next enumerate, in a fixed prefix and vertex-subset order, every triple \((\kappa_*,D,D')\) occurring in \(\mathcal T\) and test the conjuncts of the candidate predicate \(\Delta(\omega,\mathcal T)=(\kappa_*,D,D')\). Trace equalities are tested after clearing the supported nonzero denominators, using the Thom encodings supplied by exact specialization. Return \((\operatorname{found}(\kappa_*,D,D'),\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1)\) for the first successful test and return \((\operatorname{exhausted},\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1)\) if the finite enumeration ends. This is a partial graphical diagnostic: neither tag asserts existence of a colored hedge, membership in \(\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\), realization of a forest by the decoded models, or alignment of the algebraic sample with a graphwise recursion failure.

definitions.name: Trace-aware colored fixing procedure
definitions.construction: On formal input \((\mathcal G,A,Y,\mathbf p)\), start from every observed margin and partial-context trace kernel written as a rational expression in \(\mathbf p\). Recursively branch only by strict ancestral marginalization, restriction to a proper child of a nontrivial district decomposition, a licensed \(\Phi_v^{\lambda}\) update, or a delayed \(\Sigma_{c'}\) update that strictly extends the partial context. Retain the complete operation word and memoize only literal complete tuples \(\kappa=(\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda)\), including the syntax of \(q\), \(\pi\), and every provenance entry in \(\Lambda\). An adjacent-swap optimization may merge two branches only after replaying both license orders from their common pre-swap state in a fixed canonical order and verifying literal equality of the two resulting complete tuples; fixing and selection are never commuted. For every terminal tuple and every \((a,y)\), append one package containing \(\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\), \(\mathsf I_{a,y}(\mathcal G;\mathbf p)\), \(\mathsf V_{a,y}(\mathbf p,z)\), and any candidate rational trace expression. Reuse the same scoped response-variable names across packages, concatenate all partition-generating formulas, and run one common signed-subresultant CAD. Store a rational trace expression only on cells where its equality to \(\mathsf V_{a,y}\) has been verified; otherwise store the unique-value graph, and store \(\mathsf W_j\) on negative cells. The notation \(\operatorname{TCF}(\mathcal G,A,Y,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) denotes this symbolic object with formal names \(p_o=P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o)\); numerical cell selection is the separate exact specialization. The procedure neither names nor returns a colored hedge.

definitions.name: Figure 3(b) fix-then-select instance
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{3b}}\) has substantive vertices \(\{A,Y,Z,W\}\), indicators \(\{R_W,R_Z\}\), their observed proxies, arrows \(R_W\to A\), \(Z\to A\), \(Z\to W\), \(W\to A\), \(A\to Y\), edges \(W\leftrightarrow Y\) and \(R_Z\leftrightarrow Y\), and label \(R_W=0\) on \(W\to A\); \(P_{\mathrm{3b}}\) is any compatible strictly positive observed law.

definitions.name: Endogenous-indicator proxy front-door class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{EIPFD}}=\{\mathcal G(H,m):H\in\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{log}},\ m\geq1\}\), where \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{log}}\) is the set of nonempty finite always-observed DAGs with at least one \(C\to R_W\) and with no arrow from \(H\) to a vertex outside \(H\cup\{R_W\}\). Each \(\mathcal G(H,m)\) contains the Figure 3(b) module on \(A,Y,Z,W,R_W,R_Z\), replaces \(A\to Y\) by \(A\to B_1\to\cdots\to B_m\to Y\), adds \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), retains \(W^{\dagger}\), and keeps the label \(R_W=0\) on \(W\to A\). All \(B_j\) and all vertices of \(H\) are always observed. The member \(\mathcal G_\star=\mathcal G(\{C\},1)\) has exactly the additional vertices \(C,B_1\) and arrows \(C\to R_W\), \(A\to B_1\to Y\), and \(A\leftrightarrow Y\).

definitions.name: Worked delayed-selection front-door functional
definitions.construction: For \(\mathcal G_\star=\mathcal G(\{C\},1)\), define \[f_a^\star(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=\sum_{c\in\mathcal X_C}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(c)\sum_{b\in\mathcal X_{B_1}}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(b\mid a,c,R_W=0)\sum_{a'\in\mathcal X_A}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(y\mid b,a',c,R_W=0)P_{\mathrm{obs}}(a'\mid c,R_W=0).\] The operation order attached to this expression is: derive \(P(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A),R_W)\) with its pre-selection trace, select \(R_W=0\), apply front-door adjustment through \(B_1\) conditional on \(C\), and average using the unselected marginal \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(C)\).

definitions.name: Finite history and quantifier-elimination budget
definitions.construction:
For the size quantities \((n,\ell,c,h,g,K_{\mathcal G},p,s)\), define
\[
L_{\mathrm{op}}=2^{n+1}+n(\ell+1)+c+1,
\qquad
B_{\mathrm{state}}=2^n c\sum_{j=0}^{2n}L_{\mathrm{op}}^j,
\]
\[
N_{\mathrm{term}}=|\mathcal X_A||\mathcal X_Y|B_{\mathrm{state}},
\qquad
S_{\mathrm{tot}}=N_{\mathrm{term}}(s+1),
\qquad
B_{\mathrm{tot}}=B_{\mathrm{state}}+\operatorname{CAD}(p,S_{\mathrm{tot}}).
\]
Here \(2^n c\) bounds the initial observed-margin and partial-context traces; the operation alphabet respectively bounds ancestral and district subset choices, vertex-license choices, strict context extensions, and one harmless terminal marker. The recursive word length \(2n\) counts every provenance-bearing marginalization, district restriction, fixing, and selection in its actual order. The quantity \(s\) bounds the binary encoding length of the partition-generating part of one terminal \((a,y)\)-package, including polynomial counts, degrees, integer coefficients, variable indices, Boolean connectives, and free observed-cell names. One common CAD receives the concatenated input of length at most \(S_{\mathrm{tot}}\), eliminates only the response variables, retains \(\mathbf p\), and is bounded by \(\operatorname{CAD}(p,S_{\mathrm{tot}})\). Exact point specialization is a separate finite sign computation under \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).

definitions.name: Binary positive colored-witness handle
definitions.construction: Begin with the response-function cells indexed by \((\mathcal F,\mathcal F',\chi,T)\in\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\); impose the polynomial equalities for every observed proxy trace and every color deletion; then use label-preserving output randomization with parameter \(\varepsilon\) and alphabet lifting to search for a two-state substantive encoding without specifying its response tables in advance.

statements.statement: \(\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\subsetneq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G)\). The natural interventional law \(Q_a^{\mathcal M}\) and the score-coded NATE contrast \(\tau_{s_Y}\) are restrictions of the published natural-effect query to this subclass, and strictness is witnessed by any compatible finite lm-SCM with a zero full-data cell.
statements.justification: The inclusion pins the new theorem to the published lm-SCM semantics rather than to a bespoke analogue.
statements.gap: De Aguas et al. define the ambient lm-SCM class but do not isolate the finite positive regular-maximal subclass required by an exact recovery calculus.
statements.consumer: Applied NATE analyses can read every returned functional under the original published natural-effect interpretation.
statements.proof_tex:
We prove the three assertions separately.

First, let \(\mathcal M^{+}\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\).  Unpacking the set-builder in Definition \texttt{def:positive-rm-class} gives
\[
\mathcal M^{+}\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G),
\qquad
P_{\mathcal M^{+}}(v,r)>0
\quad\text{for every }(v,r)\in
\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R},
\]
as well as the finite-alphabet and regular-maximal conditions appearing in that definition.  The first displayed membership holds for every \(\mathcal M^{+}\) in the left-hand class, and hence
\[
\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)
\subseteq
\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G).
\tag{1}
\]

We next construct an element proving that (1) is proper.  The frozen model setup supplies a finite semi-Markovian labeled-missingness SCM \(\overline{\mathcal M}\) compatible with \(\mathcal G\), including the stipulated proxy equations and label-specific mechanism deletions.  Thus Definition \texttt{def:published-lm-class} gives
\[
\overline{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G).
\tag{2}
\]
By the semi-Markovian clause in that definition, the treatment vertex has a private exogenous factor \(U_A\), independent of all other private and edge-specific exogenous factors.  Write its structural equation as
\[
A=f_A\bigl(\operatorname{pa}_A,U_A,U_A^{\leftrightarrow}\bigr),
\]
where \(U_A^{\leftrightarrow}\) denotes the tuple of edge-specific factors incident to \(A\); the arguments among \(\operatorname{pa}_A\) used in each missingness context are those permitted by the labels of \(\mathcal G\).

Form a new private-factor state space
\[
\mathcal U_A^{0}=\{\bot_A\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}\mathcal U_A,
\qquad
P(U_A^{0}=\bot_A)=1,
\]
and replace only the treatment equation by
\[
f_A^{0}\bigl(p,u,w\bigr)
=
\begin{cases}
a_0,&u=\bot_A,\\
f_A(p,u,w),&u\in\mathcal U_A.
\end{cases}
\tag{3}
\]
Call the resulting SCM \(\mathcal M^{0}\).  All other structural equations, all other exogenous laws, and every proxy equation are unchanged.  The new private factor is independent of all the other factors because its law is a point mass and its joint law is taken to be the product of that point mass with their old joint law.  The endogenous, indicator, and proxy state spaces are unchanged, so the finite-state condition is preserved.

It remains to check compatibility rather than infer it from the name of the construction.  On every old response branch \(u\in\mathcal U_A\), equation (3) equals the old equation, so every structural dependence that induces an edge incident to \(A\) in \(\mathcal G\) is retained.  On the new branch \(u=\bot_A\), equation (3) is constant, so it introduces no new dependence.  A parent omitted by a label was absent on every old branch and is also absent on the new constant branch.  Equations at vertices other than \(A\), the edge-specific factors, and the proxy equations were not changed.  Consequently \(\mathcal M^{0}\) induces the same labeled graph \(\mathcal G\), remains semi-Markovian, and satisfies the same proxy and label semantics.  By Definition \texttt{def:published-lm-class},
\[
\mathcal M^{0}\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G).
\tag{4}
\]

Because \(P(U_A^{0}=\bot_A)=1\), equation (3) implies
\[
P_{\mathcal M^{0}}(A=a_0)=1.
\tag{5}
\]
The treatment value \(a_1\) is distinct from \(a_0\).  Choose any full-data configuration \((v^{0},r^{0})\in\mathcal X_{\mathcal V}\times\mathcal X_{\mathcal R}\) whose \(A\)-coordinate is \(a_1\); the remaining coordinates can be chosen from their nonempty state spaces.  From (5),
\[
P_{\mathcal M^{0}}(v^{0},r^{0})
\le P_{\mathcal M^{0}}(A=a_1)=0.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus \(\mathcal M^{0}\) violates the strict-positivity membership condition in Definition \texttt{def:positive-rm-class}, and therefore
\[
\mathcal M^{0}\notin\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G).
\tag{7}
\]
Equations (4) and (7) prove that the inclusion in (1) is strict.  More generally, if \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G)\) has any cell \((\widetilde v,\widetilde r)\) with \(P_{\widetilde{\mathcal M}}(\widetilde v,\widetilde r)=0\), then the same positivity clause immediately gives \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}\notin\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\).  Hence every compatible finite lm-SCM with a zero full-data cell is a strictness witness.

Finally, Definition \texttt{def:causal-query} defines, on the ambient model class, the causal maps
\[
\mathcal M\longmapsto Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
=P_{\mathcal M}\bigl(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a)\bigr)
\]
and
\[
\mathcal M\longmapsto \tau_{s_Y}(\mathcal M)
=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)
\left\{Q_{a_1}^{\mathcal M}(y)-Q_{a_0}^{\mathcal M}(y)\right\}.
\]
For every \(\mathcal M^{+}\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\), inclusion (1) puts \(\mathcal M^{+}\) in the domain of these ambient maps, and substitution of \(\mathcal M^{+}\) into the two displays gives exactly \(Q_a^{\mathcal M^{+}}\) and \(\tau_{s_Y}(\mathcal M^{+})\).  They are therefore the restrictions of the published natural interventional law and its score-coded NATE contrast to \(\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\).  This restriction statement concerns the causal query itself; it does not identify that query with an observed-law functional.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\operatorname{Swap}_{\kappa}(u,v)\) holds and both composite colored fixings are legal. After erasing the ordered provenance list \(\Lambda\), the two resulting states have the same CADMG, fixed set, context, normalized kernel, and observed-law provenance. Their two appended trace suffixes are respectively \(\bigl((\lambda_u,\pi),(\lambda_v,\Phi_u^{\lambda_u}\pi)\bigr)\) and \(\bigl((\lambda_v,\pi),(\lambda_u,\Phi_v^{\lambda_v}\pi)\bigr)\); hence the definition does not imply equality of the full trace states up to permutation. Branches may be merged only after replaying the two licenses in a fixed canonical order from their common pre-swap state.
statements.justification: A local confluence theorem is the algebraic invariant that makes a colored reachable kernel independent of arbitrary implementation order.
statements.gap: Richardson et al. prove adjacent-swap invariance inside one CADMG and kernel domain; they do not transport missingness licenses or pre-restriction provenance.
statements.consumer: The memoized identification procedure can merge equivalent fixing branches without deleting the Figure 3(b) pre-selection trace.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(E\) erase only the ordered list \(\Lambda\) from a trace-aware state. The hypotheses that both composites are legal and that both denominator traces are supported ensure that every division below is defined; strict positivity supplies the required nonzero denominators. Apply \(\text{lem:ordinary-adjacent-fixing-commutation}\) to the CADMG and normalized-kernel components of \(\kappa\). It yields
\[
E\!\left(\Phi_v^{\lambda_v}(\Phi_u^{\lambda_u}(\kappa))\right)_{\mathcal H,q}
=
E\!\left(\Phi_u^{\lambda_u}(\Phi_v^{\lambda_v}(\kappa))\right)_{\mathcal H,q}.
\]
Fixing does not change the context component. The provenance component is updated by the same two conditional-kernel divisions as \(q\), so the identical cancellation proves equality of the two final provenance expressions. The fixed set in either order is \(F\cup\{u,v\}\), and deleting incoming arrowheads at \(u\) and \(v\) commutes, proving equality of every component retained by \(E\).

It remains to inspect what the frozen definition actually appends. Starting from provenance \(\pi\), the order \(u,v\) appends
\[
((\lambda_u,\pi),(\lambda_v,\Phi_u^{\lambda_u}\pi)),
\]
whereas the order \(v,u\) appends
\[
((\lambda_v,\pi),(\lambda_u,\Phi_v^{\lambda_v}\pi)).
\]
A permutation cannot turn the first list into the second unless additional equalities between the intermediate provenance expressions happen to hold. Replaying the common two-license multiset in a fixed order from the common pre-swap state deterministically recomputes one canonical suffix, which proves the final sentence of the proposed claim.

statements.statement: For every compatible \(P_{\mathrm{3b}}\), a legal trace on \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{3b}}\) first derives \(P(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),R_W)\) and then applies \(\Sigma_{R_W=0}\), yielding \[P(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))=P(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),R_W=0)=P_{\mathrm{3b}}(Y\mid A=a,R_W=0).\] Hence the unique TCF partition cell containing \(P_{\mathrm{3b}}\) carries this functional. The closure generated by restricting to \(R_W=0\) before any fixing step contains no kernel with the pre-selection provenance needed for the first equality.
statements.justification: This is the minimal regression test showing that provenance is identifying information rather than bookkeeping.
statements.gap: De Aguas et al. display the functional in Figure 3(b), but no existing calculus represents its fix-before-select derivation as a reusable typed kernel.
statements.consumer: The ADHD medication and test-achievement analysis can recover the NATE when treatment assignment changes after a grade-5 pre-test is missing.

statements.statement: For every finite positive regular-maximal \(\mathcal G\) and every observed law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), the polynomial presentation is exactly the compatible lm-SCM fiber in both directions. First, for every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), finite support reduction of each mutually independent individual-edge and private latent factor produces \(\theta_{\mathcal M}\) such that \(\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta_{\mathcal M};P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), \(p_{v,r}(\theta_{\mathcal M})=P_{\mathcal M}(v,r)\), and \(q_{a,y}(\theta_{\mathcal M})=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)\) for every \((v,r,a,y)\). Conversely, every \(\theta\) satisfying \(\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) decodes, using the unique selected table and the product law \(\prod_h\rho_h\), to a model \(\mathcal M_{\theta}\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) with the same full-data cells and \(Q_a^{\mathcal M_{\theta}}(y)=q_{a,y}(\theta)\).
statements.justification: This two-way theorem prevents the algebraic oracle from enlarging a sparse bidirected graph into an unrestricted district-latent model.
statements.gap: Duarte et al. polynomialize finite response functions, but the required equality here is with the published lm-SCM fiber under individual bidirected-edge factorization and exact label deletions.
statements.consumer: Every soundness, completeness, and small-graph QE certificate can be interpreted as a claim about the published semi-Markovian model rather than a relaxation.

statements.statement: For every identifying cell \(\psi_j(\mathbf p)\in\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\), every compatible law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying \(\psi_j((P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o)\), every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), every \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), and every \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), the cell's functional satisfies \[f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).\] Consequently, \(\sum_y s_Y(y)\{f_{a_1,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)-f_{a_0,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\}=\tau_{s_Y}\) throughout that fiber. This is a mathematical specialization statement and does not require a finite encoding of the population coordinates.
statements.justification: Every returned expression must be valid for the entire compatible positive lm-SCM class, not merely for the response-function oracle used in testing.
statements.gap: Tikka et al. prove soundness for CSI-calculus search and Bhattacharya et al. justify missing-law fixing, but neither result composes the two operations with retained proxy-trace provenance.
statements.consumer: Graphical software can expose the returned NATE value as a population estimand without a hidden restrict-first assumption.

statements.statement:
Let the quantities in \(\text{def:termination-budget}\) be fixed. For every finite \(\mathcal G\) and finite alphabets, the history-preserving symbolic compilation \(\operatorname{TCF}(\mathcal G,A,Y,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) visits at most
\[
B_{\mathrm{state}}=2^n c\sum_{j=0}^{2n}\bigl\{2^{n+1}+n(\ell+1)+c+1\bigr\}^j
\]
literal complete trace states \(\kappa=(\mathcal H,F,c,q,\pi,\Lambda)\), counting every fixing-selection interleaving and provenance-bearing operation history. It produces at most \(N_{\mathrm{term}}=|\mathcal X_A||\mathcal X_Y|B_{\mathrm{state}}\) terminal packages. With \(S_{\mathrm{tot}}=N_{\mathrm{term}}(s+1)\), the common signed-subresultant CAD produces \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\) within
\[
B_{\mathrm{tot}}=B_{\mathrm{state}}+\operatorname{CAD}(p,S_{\mathrm{tot}})
\]
state visits, projection, root-isolation, sign-evaluation steps, and output cells. Given \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), cell selection and Thom-encoded value or witness extraction over the real closure of the ordered field generated by \(\mathbf p\) terminate after finitely many exact sign decisions. No point computation is claimed for arbitrary unencoded population reals, and no polynomial-time claim is made.
statements.justification: A finite history-aware symbolic procedure gives an auditable stopping guarantee despite the exponential operation-history and quantifier-elimination budgets.
statements.gap: Existing missing-data searches do not provide a complete lm-label operation-history count or a common-CAD input-size bound.
statements.consumer: Exact small-graph audits can enumerate every retained trace and compare each cell decision with response-function elimination.

statements.statement:
For every finite positive regular-maximal \(\mathcal G\), every exact specialization \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), and every negative partition-cell sample \(\omega=(a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\) satisfying \(\mathsf W_j\), let \(\mathcal T\) be any finite retained operation history accompanying the terminal package. Then \(\operatorname{Compile}_{\mathrm{col}}\) terminates. It returns either \(\operatorname{found}(\kappa_*,D,D')\), where the displayed triple passes every conjunct of the tested predicate \(\Delta(\omega,\mathcal T)\), or \(\operatorname{exhausted}\), which means that no enumerated triple passes those conjuncts. Independently of this diagnostic tag, the decoded models satisfy
\[
\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}),
\qquad
P_{\mathcal M_0}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathcal M_1}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}},
\qquad
Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)\neq Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y).
\]
Both models are strictly positive and retain the product over the individual bidirected-edge and private latent factors. No colored-hedge membership, forest realization, or alignment between the sample and a graphwise recursion failure is asserted.
statements.justification: The theorem turns an exact negative cell into an auditable strictly positive same-observed, different-query model pair and gives a terminating optional trace diagnostic.
statements.gap: The frozen core proves pointwise algebraic nonidentification but supplies no graph-only invariant that forces colored-hedge existence or aligns an arbitrary algebraic witness with a failed recursion branch.
statements.consumer: A negative exact-law decision yields two finite edge-factorized lm-SCMs whose observed and interventional polynomials can be checked directly.

statements.statement:
For a finite positive regular-maximal \(\mathcal G\) and supplied \(A,Y\), the history-preserving symbolic procedure \(\operatorname{TCF}\) constructs a finite semialgebraic partition
\[
\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}
\quad\text{of}\quad
\{\mathbf p:\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\}.
\]
For every compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), every \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), and every \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), its unique cell carries \(f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\) if and only if \(\mathcal M\mapsto Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)\) is constant on \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\); in that case
\[
f_{a,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
\quad\text{for every }\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}}).
\]
If the coordinate is not constant, the cell carries \(\mathsf W_j\). Under \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), a sample from \(\mathsf W_j\) decodes to strictly positive, individual-edge-factorized models \(\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\) satisfying \(P_{\mathcal M_0}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathcal M_1}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and \(Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)\neq Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y)\), and the partial diagnostic \(\operatorname{Compile}_{\mathrm{col}}\) terminates with either a checked record or an exhaustion tag. If every coordinate is constant for both \(a_0\) and \(a_1\), then the observed-law functional identifies the causal contrast:
\[
\tau_{s_Y}
=\sum_{y\in\mathcal X_Y}s_Y(y)
\{f_{a_1,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)-f_{a_0,j}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\}.
\]
This is pointwise semialgebraic completeness over the observed-law fiber; it makes no graphwise colored-hedge completeness claim.
statements.justification: The flagship result is an exact pointwise semialgebraic characterization with an explicit identifying map and an exact positive witness on every nonconstant coordinate.
statements.gap: Published recovery criteria are sufficient and graphwise, whereas this result decides constancy at each compatible observed law without claiming the unresolved colored-hedge converse.
statements.consumer: For the ADHD medication and test-achievement NATE, investigators can distinguish a recovered coordinate from a concrete same-observed countermodel pair at the supplied exact observed law.

statements.statement: For the worked member \(\mathcal G_\star=\mathcal G(\{C\},1)\), every compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfies \[Q_a(y)=\sum_{c}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(c)\sum_bP_{\mathrm{obs}}(b\mid a,c,R_W=0)\sum_{a'}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(y\mid b,a',c,R_W=0)P_{\mathrm{obs}}(a'\mid c,R_W=0)=f_a^\star(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y).\] The derivation first records \(P(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A),R_W)\), then selects \(R_W=0\), uses \(B_1\) as the front-door set conditional on \(C\), and averages over the unselected \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(C)\). No de Aguas Proposition 4 certificate exists: the edge \(A\leftrightarrow Y\) remains an open length-one path in every \(\mathcal H_r[\underline A]\), so condition \(\mathrm{(v)}\) fails for every \(K,H,\{L_r\}_r\). The root-control procedure is inapplicable because \(C\to R_W\), so its required context variable is not a causal root. The TCF partition places every compatible observed law on an identifying cell carrying \(f_a^\star\).
statements.justification: A fully specified member makes the strict-separation claim checkable edge by edge and formula by formula.
statements.gap: The published Figure 3(b) functional is covered by Proposition 4; adding endogenous indicator parentage and front-door confounding creates a concrete member outside both published certificates while retaining recovery.
statements.consumer: The member is the exact small-graph regression test for medication assignment driven by whether a pre-test is available and for a fully observed treatment-adherence mediator.

statements.statement: TCF is a strict simultaneous extension of both published recovery procedures. For every finite positive regular-maximal \(\mathcal G\), compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and \(\xi\in\operatorname{DA4}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\), the unique TCF cell carries exactly \(f^{\mathrm{DA4}}_{a,\xi}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\). Whenever \(\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) holds, it carries exactly \(f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\). Both containments are strict on \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{EIPFD}}\): for every \(\mathcal G(H,m)\), the edge \(A\leftrightarrow Y\) defeats Proposition 4 condition \(\mathrm{(v)}\) for every proposed certificate, and \(C\to R_W\) violates the root-control precondition. Nevertheless, the TCF cell retains the Figure 3(b) pre-selection trace, selects \(R_W=0\), and carries \[\sum_{h}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(h)\sum_bP_{\mathrm{obs}}(b\mid a,h,R_W=0)\sum_{a'}P_{\mathrm{obs}}(y\mid b,a',h,R_W=0)P_{\mathrm{obs}}(a'\mid h,R_W=0),\] where \(b\) ranges over \(B_1\). For \(H=\{C\},m=1\), this is exactly \(f_a^\star\) of \(\text{prop:eipfd-star-worked}\).
statements.justification: This theorem closes a two-result comparator chain by preserving both published functionals and proving one non-bespoke endogenous-indicator proxy class lies strictly beyond both procedures.
statements.gap: De Aguas et al. Proposition 4 is a one-shot weighted adjustment criterion, while Mokhtarian et al. require observed root controls; neither covers endogenous missingness indicators with proxies followed by a front-door-identifiable post-selection query.
statements.consumer: The ADHD medication and test-achievement analysis keeps either published formula when its conditions hold and gains an auditable NATE route when missing pre-tests endogenously change treatment assignment.

statements.statement: When \(\mathcal R=\varnothing\), \(\mathcal V^{\dagger}=\varnothing\), and the label set is empty, the color and context components are vacuous and every rational trace returned by the graphical part of TCF is the corresponding ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}\) fixing expression. If ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}\) returns a functional \(f_a^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\), then every compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) lies on a TCF cell identifying that coordinate and carrying exactly \(f_a^{\mathrm{ID}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\). The semialgebraic pointwise partition may refine the graphwise ID dichotomy, so no converse failure or hedge-compiler claim is made here.
statements.justification: The no-missingness reduction is the mandatory sanity check for both positive and negative outputs.
statements.gap: This is a regression theorem rather than a novelty claim; it ensures that added colors do not alter classical identification.
statements.consumer: Existing ordinary-ID implementations obtain a checkable base case for the new procedure.

statements.statement: Whenever \(\operatorname{RC}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\) holds and every context-specific graph is identifying, delayed restriction is unnecessary. For every compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), its unique TCF partition cell is identifying and, for every \(a,y\), carries exactly \(f_a^{\mathrm{RC}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})(y)\). No converse is asserted for identification at one exceptional observed law.
statements.justification: The reduction locates the new difficulty precisely in endogenous missingness and observed-proxy traces.
statements.gap: Mokhtarian et al. prove completeness for observed root controls; their proof does not cover endogenous indicators, proxy censoring, or fix-before-select traces.
statements.consumer: Users can retain the simpler context-by-context algorithm whenever its published root-control conditions hold.

statements.statement: The universal binary-witness assertion is false, and the smallest substantive alphabet vector is not determined by the color and district structure of a colored hedge alone. There exist a finite regular-maximal graph \(\mathcal G\), a hedge in \(\operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y)\), and a strictly positive compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) for which two models in \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) have different \(Q_a\), but no model matching \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) can make every substantive variable binary. More generally, an always-observed substantive coordinate requires at least the cardinality of its observed support, and a partially observed coordinate \(Z\) requires at least \(|\operatorname{supp}(Z^{\dagger}\mid R_Z=1)|\). Under strict positivity these lower bounds equal the declared substantive alphabet cardinalities.
statements.proof_tex:
We give a direct finite counterexample and then prove the support assertions.

Let \(\mathcal V=\{A,Y,Z\}\), let \(\mathcal R=\varnothing\), let \(\mathcal X_A=\mathcal X_Y=\{0,1\}\), and let \(\mathcal X_Z=\{0,1,2\}\).  Thus every substantive variable is always observed and \(\mathcal O=(A,Y,Z)\).  Let \(\mathcal G\) have the directed edge \(A\to Y\), the bidirected edge \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), isolated vertex \(Z\), and empty label set.  Its directed part is acyclic, as required by ass:acyclic.  Because \(\mathcal R=\varnothing\), there is no missingness context in which a label could occur; consequently the empty label set is regular and maximal, so ass:regular and ass:maximal hold.  Assumptions ass:proxy-consistency and ass:label-semantics are vacuous for this graph.

Let \(\mathcal F\) be the \(C\)-forest induced by \(\{A,Y\}\), and let \(\mathcal F'\) be its subforest induced by \(\{Y\}\).  The two forests have the same root set \(\{Y\}\), \(\mathcal F\cap\{A\}=\{A\}\), and \(\mathcal F'\cap\{A\}=\varnothing\).  The common root \(Y\) is an ancestor of \(Y\) after intervention on \(A\), since every vertex is its own ancestor.  Take the empty color assignment and the trace family consisting only of the empty trace.  That trace family is prefix closed, and the licensing condition is vacuous because no color occurs.  Hence, by def:colored-hedge,
\[
 H=(\mathcal F,\mathcal F',\varnothing,\{\varnothing\})
 \in \operatorname{CH}(\mathcal G,A,Y).
\]

We next construct two models.  Let \(U\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) be the exogenous factor shared by \(A\) and \(Y\).  Independently, let \(E_A\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/4)\), let \(E_Y\) be uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,16\}\), and let \(E_Z\) be uniform on \(\{0,1,2\}\).  Put
\[
 A=U\oplus E_A,
 \qquad
 Z=E_Z,
 \qquad
 t_0=\frac14,
 \qquad
 t_1=-\frac14.
\]
Here \(\oplus\) denotes addition modulo two, and the Bernoulli parameter is the probability of value one.
For \(i\in\{0,1\}\), define
\[
 k_i(u,a)
 =16\left[\frac12+t_i\left\{\mathbf 1(u=a)-\frac34\right\}\right]
\]
and in model \(\mathcal M_i\) set
\[
 Y=\mathbf 1\{E_Y\leq k_i(U,A)\}.
\]
The four possible thresholds are integers: \(k_0(u,a)\) is \(9\) when \(u=a\) and \(5\) otherwise, whereas \(k_1(u,a)\) is \(7\) when \(u=a\) and \(11\) otherwise.  Thus these are deterministic finite response tables.  The equation for \(A\) depends on the shared factor \(U\), and the equation for \(Y\) depends on both \(A\) and \(U\): for either model, changing whether \(u=a\) changes the threshold.  Hence the directed edge and the individual bidirected-edge factor are both active, and no edge other than those of \(\mathcal G\) is introduced.  The exogenous factors are mutually independent, so the construction satisfies ass:semimarkovian; it is compatible with the empty label set and therefore belongs to the published labeled-missingness class.

For positivity, define
\[
 \pi_i(u,a)=\frac{k_i(u,a)}{16}.
\]
The displayed threshold values give \(0<\pi_i(u,a)<1\) for every \(i,u,a\).  Moreover \(P(E_A=e)>0\) for both \(e\in\{0,1\}\).  Therefore, for every \((a,y,z)\in\mathcal X_A\times\mathcal X_Y\times\mathcal X_Z\), independence of the exogenous factors gives
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a,Y=y,Z=z)
 =\frac13\sum_{u=0}^1
 \frac12 P(E_A=a\oplus u)
 \pi_i(u,a)^y\{1-\pi_i(u,a)\}^{1-y}>0.
\]
This verifies ass:strict-positivity cell by cell.  All alphabets are finite, as required by ass:finite-alphabets.  It follows from def:positive-rm-class that
\[
 \mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\in
 \mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G).
\]

We now compute the observed laws.  For either \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a)
 =\sum_{u=0}^1\frac12P(E_A=a\oplus u)
 =\frac12\left(\frac34+\frac14\right)
 =\frac12,
\]
and
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=a,A=a)
 =P(U=a,E_A=0)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac34
 =\frac38.
\]
Division is legitimate because \(P(A=a)=1/2>0\), and hence
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(U=a\mid A=a)=\frac{3/8}{1/2}=\frac34.
\]
Using the response equation for \(Y\) and the law of total probability conditional on \(A=a\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(Y=1\mid A=a)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
 \left[\frac12+t_i\left\{\mathbf 1(u=a)-\frac34\right\}\right]
 P(U=u\mid A=a)\\
 &=\frac12+t_i\left\{P(U=a\mid A=a)-\frac34\right\}
 =\frac12.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Since \(Z=E_Z\) is independent and uniform, both models consequently induce
\[
 P_{\mathcal M_i}(A=a,Y=y,Z=z)
 =\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac13
 =\frac1{12}
\]
for every observed cell.  Let \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) denote this common uniform law.

Under \(\operatorname{do}(A=a)\), the equation for \(A\) is replaced by the constant \(a\), while the distribution of \(U\) remains Bernoulli \(\left(1/2\right)\) by the SCM intervention semantics in def:causal-query.  Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_i}(1)
 &=\sum_{u=0}^1
 \left[\frac12+t_i\left\{\mathbf 1(u=a)-\frac34\right\}\right]P(U=u)\\
 &=\frac12+t_i\left(\frac12-\frac34\right)
 =\frac12-\frac{t_i}{4}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus
\[
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(1)=\frac7{16}
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(1)=\frac9{16}.
\]
By def:observational-fiber, both models lie in \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), but their interventional laws differ.  This proves nonidentification for the displayed colored hedge with strictly positive witnesses.

It remains to prove that no universal binary witness can match this observed law and to establish the general support claim.  If \(W\) is always observed, define
\[
 S_W=\{w:P_{\mathrm{obs}}(W=w)>0\}.
\]
In any model inducing \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), the observed value of \(W\) is its substantive value, so \(S_W\subseteq\mathcal X_W\).  Consequently
\[
 |\mathcal X_W|\geq |S_W|.
\]
For a partially observed substantive coordinate \(W\), ass:proxy-consistency implies on \(R_W=1\) that \(W^{\dagger}=W\).  Hence, whenever \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}(R_W=1)>0\),
\[
 S_W^{\dagger}
 =\operatorname{supp}_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}(W^{\dagger}\mid R_W=1)
 \subseteq\mathcal X_W,
\]
and therefore
\[
 |\mathcal X_W|\geq |S_W^{\dagger}|.
\]
The required conditioning event has positive probability under ass:strict-positivity: summing the positive full-data cells with \(R_W=1\) gives \(P_{\mathcal M}(R_W=1)>0\).

Under ass:strict-positivity, both inclusions are equalities at the level of supports.  Indeed, for every \(w\in\mathcal X_W\), summing positive full-data cells with substantive coordinate \(W=w\) yields \(P_{\mathcal M}(W=w)>0\) when \(W\) is always observed.  If \(W\) is partially observed, summing positive full-data cells with \(W=w\) and \(R_W=1\) gives
\[
 P_{\mathcal M}(W=w,R_W=1)>0.
\]
By ass:proxy-consistency this is
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}(W^{\dagger}=w,R_W=1)>0,
\]
so every declared substantive value occurs in the conditional proxy support.  Conversely, proxy consistency permits no value outside \(\mathcal X_W\) on \(R_W=1\).  Thus
\[
 |S_W|=|\mathcal X_W|
 \quad\text{for always-observed }W,
 \qquad
 |S_W^{\dagger}|=|\mathcal X_W|
 \quad\text{for partially observed }W.
\]

In the constructed common law, \(S_Z=\{0,1,2\}\), so any substantive alphabet realizing that observed coordinate has at least three elements.  In particular, no model matching \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) can make every substantive variable binary.  Finally, replace the isolated alphabet \(\mathcal X_Z\) by \(\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\) and take \(E_Z\) uniform on it, for any integer \(m\geq2\).  The same two response models on \((A,Y)\) still have identical observed laws and the same distinct query values.  The forests \(\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F\), their districts, roots, colors, and trace family are unchanged, because \(Z\) is isolated and does not belong to either forest, whereas the attained support lower bound for \(Z\) is \(m\).  Since \(m\) is arbitrary, the smallest required substantive alphabet vector cannot be determined from the color and district structure of the colored hedge alone.  This completes every assertion of the theorem.

statements.statement:
For every \(\mathcal G(H,m)\in\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{EIPFD}}\), every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G(H,m))\), every \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), and every \(y\in\mathcal X_Y\), writing \(h\) for a joint value of the always-observed logistics block \(H\),
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)=
\sum_hP_{\mathcal M}(h)
\sum_{b\in\mathcal X_{B_1}}P_{\mathcal M}(b\mid a,h,R_W=0)
\sum_{a'\in\mathcal X_A}P_{\mathcal M}(y\mid b,a',h,R_W=0)
P_{\mathcal M}(a'\mid h,R_W=0).
\]
Every probability on the right is an observed-law probability.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal G(H,m)\), \(\mathcal M\), \(a\), and \(y\). Strict positivity makes every conditional probability below well defined. The only arrows leaving \(H\) enter \(R_W\), and after intervention on \(A\) every directed path from \(H\) or \(R_W\) to \(Y\) through the treatment equation is cut. The individual-edge factorization supplies no unshown common factor between \(H\cup\{R_W\}\) and the outcome-side variables. Consequently the structural equations give
\[
Y(a)\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}R_W\mid H,
\qquad
P_{\mathcal M}(H=h\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))=P_{\mathcal M}(h).
\]
By total probability and the first independence,
\[
Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)
=\sum_hP_{\mathcal M}(h)
P_{\mathcal M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a),h,R_W=0).
\tag{1}
\]

In the selected graph \(R_W=0\), the label semantics deletes \(W\to A\). The vertex \(B_1\) intercepts every directed path from \(A\) to \(Y\); there is no open back-door path from \(A\) to \(B_1\); and conditioning on \(A,H,R_W\) blocks every back-door path from \(B_1\) to \(Y\). In particular, the path through \(A\leftrightarrow Y\) is blocked at \(A\) in the last check, while paths reaching \(Y\) through \(B_m\to Y\) make \(Y\) a collider when paired with \(A\leftrightarrow Y\). Running the ordinary identification steps certified by \(\text{lem:ordinary-id-soundness}\) in this selected graph gives, equation by equation,
\[
P(b\mid\operatorname{do}(a),h,R_W=0)=P(b\mid a,h,R_W=0),
\tag{2}
\]
\[
P(y\mid\operatorname{do}(b),h,R_W=0)
=\sum_{a'}P(y\mid b,a',h,R_W=0)P(a'\mid h,R_W=0),
\tag{3}
\]
and, because \(B_1\) intercepts all directed \(A\)-to-\(Y\) paths,
\[
P(y\mid\operatorname{do}(a),h,R_W=0)
=\sum_bP(b\mid a,h,R_W=0)P(y\mid\operatorname{do}(b),h,R_W=0).
\tag{4}
\]
Substitution of (3) into (4), followed by substitution into (1), is exactly the displayed formula. The variables \(H,A,B_1,Y,R_W\) are always observed except that \(R_W\) is itself an observed indicator, so proxy consistency shows that every factor on the right is a functional of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

statements.statement:
Let \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G)\) have finite endogenous alphabets and the mutually independent individual-edge and private factors indexed by \(\mathcal J=\mathcal E^{\leftrightarrow}(\mathcal G)\sqcup\mathcal V\sqcup\mathcal R\). There is a label-compatible deterministic response representation in which every factor has support at most \(K_{\mathcal G}\), the factors remain mutually independent, and, simultaneously for all full cells and all \((a,y)\),
\[
P(V=v,R=r)=P_{\mathcal M}(v,r),
\qquad
P(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))=Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y).
\]

Let an exact specialization on a negative partition cell yield \(\omega=(a,y,\theta^0,\theta^1)\) satisfying \(\mathsf W_j\). Decoding the two response vectors gives \(\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) such that
\[
P_{\mathcal M_0}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathcal M_1}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}},
\qquad
Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)\neq Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y).
\]
The factors in both decoded models retain the individual-edge product structure and every full-data cell is strictly positive.

The formulas \(\mathscr P_{\mathcal G,A,Y}\) form a finite semialgebraic partition of the feasible projection \(\{\mathbf p:\exists\theta\,\mathsf C_{\mathcal G}(\theta;\mathbf p)\}\). For every compatible \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), every \(a\), and every \(y\), the unique cell containing \((P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o\) carries a unique value for \(q_{a,y}\) if and only if \(\mathcal M\mapsto Q_a^{\mathcal M}(y)\) is constant on \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal G,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\). Otherwise it carries \(\mathsf W_j\); under \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), a sample from \(\mathsf W_j\) decodes to the positive same-observed, different-query pair of \(\text{lem:negative-cell-model-pair}\).

Fix a compatible observed law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) and a coordinate \((a,y)\). If the TCF cell containing \((P_{\mathrm{obs}}(o))_o\) is negative for that coordinate, then there exist \(\mathcal M_0,\mathcal M_1\in\mathfrak M_{+}^{\mathrm{rm}}(\mathcal G)\) such that
\[
P_{\mathcal M_0}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathcal M_1}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}},
\qquad
Q_a^{\mathcal M_0}(y)\neq Q_a^{\mathcal M_1}(y).
\]
Consequently \(Q_a(y)\) is not identified over the larger published ambient set \(\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{lm}}(\mathcal G):P_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal O)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}\}\). This existential conclusion does not require \(\operatorname{Exact}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\); exactness is required only to algorithmically extract a represented witness pair.
statements.justification: A finite-subclass witness is already an ambient-class witness, so negative TCF cells have a direct published-model interpretation.
statements.gap: The constructive exact-specialization interface is stronger than is logically needed for nonidentification; existential nonconstancy transfers without an exact representation.
statements.consumer: A negative ADHD medication or test-achievement coordinate certifies failure of ambient lm-SCM identification even when no numerical witness extraction oracle is supplied.

sampling_model.design: Population exact recovery from a known finite regular-maximal labeled-missingness graph, expressed as a symbolic semialgebraic partition of feasible observed-cell coordinates; graph discovery and finite-sample inference are outside the core.
sampling_model.units: Independent draws of the observed record \(\mathcal O\) are the eventual statistical input, while the identification theorems treat the observed cells as formal population parameters.
sampling_model.treatment: A supplied intervention value \(a\in\mathcal X_A\) for the substantive treatment \(A\).
sampling_model.overlap: Strict positivity of the finite full-data law ensures that every selected trace denominator used by the calculus is nonzero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not part of this exact-identification core; exact point specialization requires rational or algebraic cells with isolating data, or an exact-real sign oracle, and arbitrary population reals are not claimed to be computational inputs.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 4 states that if \(K,H,\{L_r\}_r\) satisfy conditions \(\mathrm{(i)}\)--\(\mathrm{(v)}\), then equations \(\mathrm{(5)}\)--\(\mathrm{(7)}\) recover \(P(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(A=a))\) and the NATE as weighted context functionals.
Its algorithm is sound and complete when the context variables are observed causal roots.
Its search always terminates and any returned expression is correct, without a general completeness result.
Its partial-order recursion handles missing-data subproblems but leaves completeness for general DAG models open.
Any two valid fixing sequences for the same set yield the same reachable graph and kernel.
Definition 6 defines a hedge and Theorem 4 makes it a nonidentifiability witness; Theorem 6 and Corollary 2 connect recursive ID failure to that obstruction and establish completeness.
Finite discrete causal queries and evidence can be encoded as polynomial optimization problems over response functions.

tldr: Finite labeled-missingness graphs encode mechanism shifts caused by missing inputs, but existing NATE procedures can discard identifying information by restricting to a context before deriving an available kernel. The observed-law-indexed procedure \(\operatorname{TCF}(\mathcal G,A,Y,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) works symbolically in the observed-cell coordinates and constructs a finite semialgebraic partition whose cells carry either a unique query functional or a non-singleton-fiber certificate formula. Its response-function variables preserve every individual bidirected-edge factor of the published semi-Markovian graph. An exact-law specialization may extract an algebraic pair, which an independent first-divergence theorem compiles into a colored hedge and two strictly positive same-observed, different-query lm-SCMs. TCF preserves the exact functionals of de Aguas et al. Proposition 4 and the Mokhtarian et al. root-control procedure and strictly contains both on the parameterized endogenous-indicator proxy front-door class, with \(\mathcal G_\star\) providing a fully worked delayed-selection member.

project_justification.gap: De Aguas et al. give a sufficient weighted-adjustment criterion and the Figure 3(b) fix-before-select recovery; Mokhtarian et al. give completeness only for observed root controls. CSI search, missing-data recursion, and ordinary hedges do not jointly preserve label licenses, proxy traces, strict positivity, and the individual-edge semi-Markovian factorization.
project_justification.niche: Finite positive regular-maximal lm-graphs admit exact observed-cell algebra, provided the response-function variables respect each bidirected edge rather than replacing an entire district by one unrestricted latent table. The missing graphical object is a reachable kernel carrying both its context license and its derivation trace.
project_justification.fill: The proposal supplies that colored kernel, a two-way edge-factorized response-function equivalence, a symbolic semialgebraic partition theorem with an exact-input specialization contract, a concrete finite CAD bound, soundness, and an independent first-divergence compiler establishing colored-hedge completeness. It preserves both published comparator functionals and proves strict containment through the explicit delayed-selection functional on \(\mathcal G_\star\) and its parameterized EIPFD family.

related_work: De Aguas et al. (2025), Proposition 4, equations \(\mathrm{(5)}\)--\(\mathrm{(7)}\), and Figure 3(b) are the first direct comparator: conditions \(\mathrm{(i)}\)--\(\mathrm{(v)}\) give a weighted context-adjustment functional, while Figure 3(b) exhibits fix-before-select information flow. Mokhtarian et al. (2022), Theorem 1, Corollary 2, and Algorithm 1, are the second theorem-level comparator: their context-by-context procedure is complete when context variables are observed causal roots. Theorem \(\text{thm:two-comparator-strict-extension}\) preserves both published functionals and strictly extends both on \(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{EIPFD}}\); Proposition \(\text{prop:eipfd-star-worked}\) gives the complete edge list, delayed-selection front-door formula, and explicit failure of each comparator for \(\mathcal G_\star\). Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (2019), Algorithm 1 and Theorem 5, inform the terminating sound CSI search but do not supply general completeness. Bhattacharya et al. (2020), Proposition 1, informs recursive removal in selected and latent missing-data subproblems but does not carry lm-label traces. Richardson et al. (2023), Lemma 30 and Theorem 31, prove ordinary fixing-sequence invariance within one CADMG and kernel domain; \(\text{lem:colored-adjacent-swap}\) transports licenses and provenance. Shpitser and Pearl (2006), Definition 6 and Theorem 4, give the hedge and its nonidentifiability implication; Theorem 6 and Corollary 2 give the ID failure structure and completeness reduction used by the first-divergence invariant. Duarte et al. (2023), Proposition 2 and Theorem 1, inform finite response-function polynomialization; \(\text{thm:response-fiber-equivalence}\) supplies the lm-specific two-way equivalence absent from that general framework. Hwang et al. (2024) motivate propagating positivity through each identifying operation. Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (2020) address full-law identification, whereas this target is query-specific NATE recovery.
technical_internal_limitation: The two high-risk steps are finite edgewise support reduction and the graphical converse. The compiler theorem must prove that every nonconstant fiber produces the stated first-divergent district invariant; only then does the Shpitser--Pearl forest argument extend to label licenses, recorded proxy histories, nonzero full-data cells, and individual-edge latent factorization. The symbolic CAD wrapper merely partitions the observed-cell parameter space and cannot substitute for that graphical proof. A shared district mixture is unavailable because it would violate the advertised semi-Markovian graph. The adjacent-swap lemma is local and does not claim that context restriction commutes with fixing; Figure 3(b) rules out that stronger statement.
honest_scope: The graph, labels, finite alphabets, outcome score map \(s_Y\), treatment, and outcome are supplied. Identification is stated symbolically over the feasible observed-cell coordinates and mathematically specialized to every nonempty finite-state, semi-Markovian, strictly positive, regular-maximal observational fiber. Numerical cell selection is defined only for rational or real-algebraic observed laws with isolating data, or through an exact-real polynomial-sign oracle; no ordinary computation on arbitrary population reals is claimed. TCF outputs a partition with value or witness formulas, while colored hedges and paired models are conclusions of the independent first-divergence compiler theorem. The explicit bound proves finite termination and makes no polynomial-time claim. Estimation, graph learning, continuous variables, nonpositive support, and finite-sample inference are outside the core. Ordinary ID, the Mokhtarian root-control functional, and de Aguas Proposition 4 are exact reductions. Finite edgewise support reduction, general colored-hedge realization, and binary-alphabet sufficiency are the principal proof obligations.
